decision: Four lanes ordered by the next carrier cutoff, one 56 px action per card
why: Counter staff work standing, often gloved, mid-conversation; the card should answer only 'what do I do next with this order'.
alternative: A sortable table of orders with a detail page per row.
value: No hunting for the right button during a rush; the lane itself is the to-do list.

decision: Store portal is offline-first: actions queue with idempotency keys
why: Mall Wi-Fi drops; a scan or handover must never be lost or double-applied when it syncs.
alternative: Block the UI with a spinner until the API answers.
value: Staff keep serving customers during outages, and replays are safe by construction.

decision: New orders arrive over a Broadcast channel, not polling
why: The lane must change within a second of checkout so pickers start before the customer arrives.
alternative: Poll the orders API every 30 seconds.
value: Two tabs, two tablets, one truth; the demo driver runs only while someone is watching, so the free tier stays idle.

decision: The cutoff agent only proposes; a person applies the plan
why: Re-routing orders has cost and customer impact, and the shift lead knows context the model does not.
alternative: Let the agent reassign pickers and carriers automatically.
value: Fast suggestions with an audit trail; trust is earned per plan instead of assumed.

decision: The carrier cutoff is a pulsing chip in the chrome, always visible
why: Every decision on this screen is relative to the next truck; hiding it in a panel makes staff re-derive urgency.
alternative: Show the cutoff only inside each order's detail.
value: Urgency is shared context, not something each person recomputes.

decision: The delivery that left the store keeps a live courier ETA and progress bar on its card, the pattern popularized by ride-hailing apps, with a link to the customer's view
why: 'Where is my order?' calls land at the counter; staff should see exactly what the customer sees, from the same run and clock.
alternative: Drop orders from view once the carrier collects them.
value: Staff answer ETA questions without leaving the board, and the answer matches the app.
